transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-06-18
Start: 14:00 PDT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Blake (Redwood AE), Marcus Li (Redwood SE), Priya Raman (Redwood Solutions), Liam Ortega (Redwood Product), Aisha Khan (NimbusCloud Head of Partnerships), Tom Reyes (Nimbus Marketplace PM), Victor Chen (Nimbus Cloud Integrations), Elena Moro (Nimbus Security)

Summary:
Short technical sync to map out marketplace listing requirements and a joint reference architecture for a managed Redwood offering in the Nimbus marketplace. Focus on packaging, network/topology (VPC), security/compliance artifacts, billing/pricing model, and a performance baseline for listing collateral.

Topics:
- Marketplace asset checklist and accepted formats
- Reference architecture (hosted vs dedicated vs private listing models)
- Networking: VPC peering / PrivateLink / transit considerations
- Security artifacts: SOC2, SAML/SSO flows, KMS, audit logs
- Packaging: Marketplace SKU, onboarding flow, automated provisioning
- Joint go-to-market assets and timelines

Action items (captured from notes): see metadata action_items above.

Transcript:
[00:00] Sofia (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We planned a short agenda — ref arch, marketplace assets, perf baseline, and next steps. Quick intros?
[00:12] Aisha (Nimbus): Hi, Aisha here — I run partnerships. Tom and Victor from the marketplace and integrations teams are on. Elena from security too.
[00:20] Tom (Nimbus): Yep, Tom, PM for Nimbus marketplace. Looking to understand what we need to list a managed Redwood offering in our catalog.
[00:27] Marcus (Redwood SE): Marcus — I'll cover the technical details: network, provisioning, and perf. Quick flag: we have three recommended listing models: Hosted API (Redwood-hosted), Dedicated (reserved pools for customers), and Private (VPC/on-prem).
[00:41] Victor (Nimbus): When you say Dedicated, are we talking about reserved GPUs that we host or Redwood hosts?
[00:47] Priya (Redwood): Great question. Dedicated in our terms is reserved capacity in Redwood's infra that we can dedicate to a tenant; can also be mapped to a Nimbus-managed VM/GPU if we do a private deployment. There's some nuance here — for marketplace listing we can offer both a "Redwood Managed" SKU and a "Bring-Your-Own" or co-managed SKU.
[01:05] Elena (Nimbus): Security-wise, we need to know what evidence you can surface: SOC2 report, encryption at rest keys, KMS integration, and whether logs can be forwarded to our SIEM.
[01:15] Marcus (Redwood): We can provide SOC2 and a security whitepaper. For KMS we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations; logs can be exported via our audit log streaming. Note: sometimes the transcription here says "KV cash" when we meant KV cache — sorry, mumble — we'll provide the right term in the doc.
[01:32] Tom (Nimbus): For the marketplace listing process, we have an asset checklist: product icon, 1-page overview, architecture diagram, security questionnaire, pricing matrix, and a deployment playbook. Does Redwood have a canonical reference arch diagram we can use?
[01:42] Priya (Redwood): We do. I'll draft a reference architecture showing the three deployment patterns and flow for onboarding through the marketplace. That will show network paths for VPC peering vs PrivateLink and where KV cache and prefix caching sits in the runtime path.
[01:57] Aisha (Nimbus): Ideal. Also want to talk about billing flows: is billing done through Nimbus marketplace billing or does Redwood invoice the customer directly?
[02:05] Liam (Redwood Product): Two options: marketplace-billed (where Nimbus charges the customer and remits a cut) or passthrough where we bill directly. For a first pass listing we recommend marketplace-billed for ease of purchase; we can support both.
[02:17] Victor (Nimbus): We prefer marketplace-billed to keep UX simple. Will need to validate meter reporting — token usage, embeddings units, and peak throughput metrics.
[02:26] Marcus (Redwood): Our usage reporting can emit token counts, embedding counts, and per-route latency histograms. We'll need to map your meter schema. Marcus: action to produce a mapping doc.
[02:36] Tom (Nimbus): On the tech integration side, provisioning matters. Can the marketplace call an API to spin up a dedicated pool?
[02:41] Priya (Redwood): Yes. We have a provisioning API for Dedicated and Private that accepts a desired capacity, model version, and networking options (VPC id, subnet, CIDR). The only manual step is if it's an on-prem appliance that requires arrangement. For hosted and dedicated we can automate via API.
[02:58] Elena (Nimbus): For SSO/SAML: we need a way for tenant admins to link their SSO to Redwood console — can that be driven programmatically post-provision?
[03:05] Marcus (Redwood): Yes, SAML configs can be pushed through our control plane APIs and we support IdP-initiated and SP-initiated flows. We also support SCIM for user provisioning when requested.
[03:15] Aisha (Nimbus): Great. Any gotchas around networking — NAT, egress, and data residency?
[03:22] Priya (Redwood): Data residency can be solved by deploying dedicated capacity in region; for VPC peering we'll exchange routes, for PrivateLink we use interface endpoints. Small note: sometimes our docs say "VPC pairing" — that's incorrect term, should be peering. We'll make sure language is consistent.
[03:37] Tom (Nimbus): Marketplace also requires a short demo video and a sandbox experience. Is there a lightweight sandbox you can offer so customers can click-to-try?
[03:44] Liam (Redwood): We can provide a sandbox tier with usage limits; it can be a hosted API key tied to a sandbox account and prepopulated prompts. We'll include that in the asset list.
[03:53] Victor (Nimbus): On the reference architecture diagram, we need clear labels for certificates, KMS flow, and audit log routing. Can you show where audit logs go and how they can be forwarded to our SIEM?
[04:02] Priya (Redwood): On the diagram we'll show audit log streaming endpoint and a small agent or forwarding mechanism. We also support push to S3 or direct syslog export depending on customer reqs.
[04:11] Tom (Nimbus): One item: marketplace security review requires us to complete a security scan and provide a contact for penetration testing coordination. Who on Redwood handles that?
[04:20] Sofia (Redwood): Elena? sorry — Priya, Marcus, I think Marcus will be the security contact for the integration reviews and Elena on Nimbus will coordinate. Marcus: confirm and we'll add to action items.
[04:30] Marcus (Redwood): Confirmed. I'll be the point for the technical security review and coordinate pen-test scheduling if needed.
[04:36] Elena (Nimbus): Cool. Also, for compliance we sometimes need a 3rd party attestation or specific language in the listing — can you provide templated copy for the marketplace listing that includes compliance callouts?
[04:45] Priya (Redwood): Yes, we'll include standard compliance snippets (SOC2 type II, data in-transit and at-rest encryption, optional CMK support).
[04:52] Tom (Nimbus): About pricing: we need a clean SKU model. For example, a base subscription + per-token overage or a pure usage model. Any recommended defaults?
[04:59] Liam (Redwood): Typical: Base monthly for reserved capacity + per-token variable cost; for fully hosted SaaS we support pure usage. For marketplace it's easier to present two SKUs: Sandbox (free tier) and Managed (monthly + usage).
[05:10] Aisha (Nimbus): Let's capture that and prototype the listing page.
[05:14] Sofia (Redwood): Quick technical deep dive: latency SLOs — if a customer uses dedicated pool we can hit 50-100ms p50 on short sequences for smaller models; for larger context/longer tokens latency will be higher. We should call out the model families and expected latency in the listing.
[05:30] Marcus (Redwood): Also need to call out quantization options and GPU types because some customers care about FP16 vs INT8 and the inference quality tradeoffs. We'll include recommended model/quant profiles per SKU.
[05:42] Victor (Nimbus): For promoted listings, Nimbus requires performance claims to be backed by a reproducible benchmark. Can Redwood provide a reproducible runbook and dataset?
[05:50] Priya (Redwood): Yes, we'll provide a small benchmark harness and a reproducible prompt set so Nimbus can replicate the numbers. Marcus will run a canonical baseline on our dedicated pool and share results.
[05:58] Tom (Nimbus): On operations: we want autoscaling visibility so customers know how burst capacity is handled. Are there throttles or queueing that should be surfaced?
[06:06] Marcus (Redwood): We'll document autoscale policy: min/max pool sizes, burst allowances, and fallback model variants if capacity is constrained. We'll also document circuit-breakers and error codes.
[06:17] Aisha (Nimbus): Marketplace listing also needs support info: SLAs and support contacts for initial onboarding.
[06:22] Sofia (Redwood): We'll provide an enterprise support contact and a standard SLA summary. For marketplace we can provide a 99.9% uptime target for dedicated SKUs and best-effort for sandbox.
[06:33] Victor (Nimbus): One more item — legal/contract side. Nimbus requires a reseller or marketplace agreement signature. Who handles that?
[06:39] Sofia (Redwood): Our partnerships team handles marketplace agreements; I'll loop in legal after we agree on packaging. For now we can start with the tech integration.
[06:47] Tom (Nimbus): Great. Anything else on the reference architecture?
[06:51] Priya (Redwood): We'll sketch the diagram to include: control plane (Redwood), data plane (in-region GPUs), network hops (VPC peering or PrivateLink), KMS flow, logging, and provisioning API endpoints.
[06:59] Aisha (Nimbus): Timeline — we'd like a first draft listing by end of June and a pilot listing live in July if possible.
[07:06] Sofia (Redwood): Sounds reasonable. We'll aim to get the refarch and listing copy by 2025-06-25. Marcus will run the perf baseline and deliver by early July.
[07:14] Marcus (Redwood): Noted — I'll run the perf on 6/26 and share results by 7/2.
[07:20] Elena (Nimbus): I'll start the security intake and share the Nimbus questionnaire today.
[07:24] Tom (Nimbus): We'll also send the marketplace asset template and required image dimensions.
[07:29] Sofia (Redwood): Awesome. Quick recap of next steps...
[07:32] Sofia (Redwood): Priya to draft refarch diagram (due 6/25). Tom to send Nimbus asset checklist (due 6/23). Marcus to run perf baseline (run 6/26, share 7/2). Elena to start security questionnaire and send to Marcus (due 6/24). Redwood to prepare initial listing copy and pricing mockups (Sofia/Liam) for review week of 6/30.
[07:54] Tom (Nimbus): That works. One logistical note: for the provisioning API we may need a sandbox API key scoped to test dedicated provisioning — can you create that?
[08:03] Priya (Redwood): Yes, we can issue a scoped sandbox API key; I'll add that to the action items.
[08:09] Aisha (Nimbus): Thanks all, this was productive. We'll reconvene after we have the draft assets.
[08:15] Sofia (Redwood): Thanks everyone. We'll follow up by email and create a shared folder for artifacts.

End transcript.

Post-call notes (auto): minor transcription artefacts present (names and acronyms occasionally mistranscribed). Follow metadata for action items and next steps.
